reading_status: Two source-informed model reads of Gonur Figure 41; one source-informed model read of Altyn Depe Plate 94.2. No blinded reader or human epigraphic validation.

gonur.caption_relationship: Panel 1 depicts tokens, panel 2 depicts signs on them; group-level correspondence only.
gonur.source_find_location: one chamber by the palace's central northern entrance
gonur.source_bag_status: author proposes possible placement in one small bag

photo_panel.reading: Most outlines are rounded or oval; several are tapered or irregular. Surface marks include intersecting straight grooves and curves. The single photographed view per displayed position leaves depth and the full surface of each physical object unresolved.

drawing_panel.reading: Several drawings contain crossed straight lines forming grids; others contain curves or rounded outlines. No per-object identifiers connect the drawing positions to the photographs.

gonur.difference_interpretation: The representation count is three below the reported hoard total. Selection, repeated views, omitted specimens and individual correspondences are not documented in this figure.

second_model_check.status: source-informed independent recount of the same native page

gonur.published_function: Sarianidi proposes archive counters and checking food/cattle at the entrance; this is the excavator's interpretation.

altyn_depe.publication: L. B. Kircho, G. F. Korobkova, V. M. Masson. The technical and technological potential of the Eneolithic population of Altyn-Depe as the basis of the rise of an early urban civilization. Proceedings of IIMK RAS XXVIII. St Petersburg: European House, 2008. ISBN 9785801502489.
altyn_depe.chapter: L. B. Kircho, The Manufacturing Technology and Typology of Clay Objects at Altyn-Depe in the Eneolithic Period (Russian section begins p.72; English section p.109)
altyn_depe.view_relationship: Dashes link marked face, edge/profile and opposite face under the one item label 2.
altyn_depe.image_kind: published line drawing; no original object photograph recovered
altyn_depe.marked_face_reading: An irregular rounded surface bears two main horizontal bands of narrow elongated impressions, with additional partial impressions along the top edge. Individual cavity boundaries are ambiguous where lines meet or run into the margin.
altyn_depe.profile_reading: A tapering wedge-like profile has greater thickness toward its lower end.
altyn_depe.opposite_face_reading: The opposite view has a largely plain interior with stippling and short irregular lines; no second organized mark series is coded.

relative_chronology.reading: Excavation 5 horizons 13-9 belong to the Late Eneolithic; horizons 11-9 are attributed to later phases of the Geoksyur-type complex.
relative_chronology.regional_period_range: The book places Namazga III broadly at 3200/3100-2800/2700 BCE (printed p.6).

associated_room_items.same_plate_caption: Plate94 items1-17 are presented as room18 terracotta objects; items3 and6 are figurines-dibs.
associated_room_items.individual_floor_or_deposit_joins: The room18 narrative distinguishes multiple floors and construction/fill deposits (pp.34-36); the caption gives no corresponding subdeposit for item2.
